sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the parties have submitted that the dispute inter-se the parties is matrimonial in nature.
It is further submitted that the parties without any coercion or influence have entered into a compromise.
Hence, both the parties have jointly agreed for quashing the impugned FIRs and any further proceedings, arising therefrom.
3. Both the parties

have marked presence before the Court, Smt. Neeru Meena has apologized to Shri Lokesh Meena qua the [2024:RJ-JP:38482] (4 of 4) [CRLMP-1925/2024] discomfort caused to him on account of the aforementioned proceedings/custody period.

4. Heard and considered.
5.

At this juncture, this Court deems it appropriate to place reliance upon the dictum of the Hon'ble Apex Court enunciated in Jasmair Singh Vs. State of Haryana [(2022) 9 SCC 73] and Gian Singh Vs.
State of Punjab [(2012) 10 SCC 303], wherein, it was held that a case was eminently suitable to be considered for exercise of jurisdiction under Section 528 of BNSS for quashing of criminal proceedings, if the parties have buried the hatchet and decided to give quietus to the proceedings,
which were lodged inter se against one another.
6.

entities.text: Jasmair Singh Vs. State of Haryana [(2022) 9 SCC 73]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Gian Singh Vs.
State of Punjab [(2012) 10 SCC 303]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In view of the said legal position, laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in aforementioned cases,
and considering the fact that the dispute deals in personam and has amicably been settled between/by the parties, this Court deems it appropriate to allow the present misc. Petition.
The compromise is taken on record.
7. Considering the aforementioned, the present criminal miscellaneous petitions are allowed and the abovestated FIRs with all consequential proceedings, are hereby quashed and set aside.
